script: Emergency clothing cannot be put through expenses.. A while back I was working away from home and just going home at the weekends. I was staying in a hotel, packing only enough clothes for the week. When the call came, I was like, "Fine, I'll roll with it." but here's the thing… They wanted me to work the weekend too, so that meant two weeks solid and only one week's worth of clothes. I checked my bag, counted the socks, the underwear, the shirts – it was a bare minimum. If I didn't get new ones, I'd be stuck in the same old pair for a month, and trust me, that was not my vibe. what I didn't know was… I told the boss I needed fresh underwear and socks; I'd make do with other clothes. He said, "No, expenses won't cover that." I was like, "So what, I just wear the same ones forever?" and that's when everything changed… Malicious compliance became my game plan. I stuffed the entire bag of clothes into the hotel laundry bag. Every pair of socks and underwear was £5, each shirt and trouser £10. but here's the thing… The total hit £120, while I'd only spent £20 on the actual new gear. I filled out the expense form, typed in the numbers, and hit submit. I felt the rush of outsmarting a bureaucracy that thought it could control me. what I didn't know was… If this hadn't worked, I'd have been living in a single wardrobe for weeks. Now I was paying double the cost for a lesson in creative accounting. I could have just bought the new gear, but I wanted a bigger payoff. but here's the thing… The hotel staff looked confused as I walked out with a bag full of laundry. I laughed, because I'd just turned a petty boss into a punchline. I learned that when policies are weak, you can turn them into your own advantage. The end.
